title: WS9 row S12 (provider alias switch) vs our llm-proxy — same-wire alias-identity row: ACP session starts on claude-sonnet-4-5 (dash alias, messages wire) for 2 turns, then an in-session /model flip to claude-sonnet-4.5 (dot alias, messages wire — a SEPARATE catalog row aliasing the same underlying model/deployment) for 2 turns. This is the .75 AFFINITY-POLICY boundary question in alias form: both alias rows resolve to the same litellm deployment (the encrypted_content boundary markers encode the deployment model_id — same marker = same boundary), so the same-boundary KEEP policy (.75: 'same-boundary KEEP is PROVEN safe', proxy-capability-matrix §3.4) expects the post-switch request to RETAIN the foreign thinking blocks (T0 native-replay class on the xwfix ladder — same model+wire+encryption boundary). Verdict semantics (TOLERANT, CROSSWIRE-1 discipline — the acceptable outcomes are enumerated): PASS = the alias resolved (post-switch request carries body.model=claude-sonnet-4.5), the post-switch request is accepted (200), and the thinking blocks SURVIVED the alias switch (same-boundary KEEP — the .75 expectation). FINDING (designed-delta class, adjudicate S0 vs S2 on review) = 200 but the thinking blocks were STRIPPED at the alias switch — if the boundary markers are IDENTICAL across the switch, the strip treated a same-boundary identity as foreign = persistent user-visible fidelity loss (S2 candidate → PROP via the .75 lineage); if the markers DIFFER (the alias rows actually resolve to different deployments), the strip was justified (S0 documented delta) — the boundary-marker recon discriminates. FINDING (S1 self-healing) = 400 -> strip+retry -> 200 (the reactive net fired once; the count pin discriminates). FAIL (S3 report-and-stop) = retry storm (>=3 post-switch requests) or an unrecovered acp_error. The control pin (thinking rode pre-switch) is a premise: 0-hit => VACUOUS (the model produced no thinking to project — temperament). No expected_red: the switch mechanism is proven (RT-CROSSWIRE1/1B); the affinity-KEEP expectation is the .75 policy of record. No golden pin (the golden wire-assert kind is pending — JIG ratchet 1); the first post-switch request is the recorded fixture (recon).

steps.note: BOUNDARY-DISCRIMINATOR (S12 review step): the encrypted_content boundary markers (encitem_*/litellm_enc: forms) in the pre-switch (claude-sonnet-4-5) vs post-switch (claude-sonnet-4.5) requests — IDENTICAL markers = same deployment = same boundary (the strip, if any, is an S2 candidate via the .75 lineage); DIFFERENT markers = different deployments = the strip was justified (S0 documented delta). Read from the wire capture on review; this note names the evidence so the verdict is a step, not a guess.

ndjson.label: SESSION SURVIVES THE ALIAS SWITCH: the post-switch turns did not die (200 directly, or 400 recovered by the reactive strip).
POST-SWITCH TURN COMPLETES: the final turn on the dot-alias row delivered the exact terminal text.

wire.label: CONTROL (anti-vacuous pin): a pre-switch dash-alias request carried a thinking block — real thinking content exists to cross the alias boundary. Without this, the KEEP/strip pins are vacuous (the model produced no thinking to project).
ALIAS RESOLVED: the post-switch request carries body.model=claude-sonnet-4.5 (the dot-alias row) on /v1/messages — the alias switch actually flipped the resolved model row (same wire, same family).

SAME-BOUNDARY KEEP (the .75 expectation, T0 native-replay class): the FIRST post-switch dot-alias request (last:0 = oldest dot-alias request = the first post-switch turn) RETAINS the pre-switch thinking blocks — same deployment, same boundary, KEEP is the policy of record (proxy-capability-matrix §3.4). Absent here = the strip finding (adjudicate S0 vs S2 via the boundary-marker recon note).

NO RETRY STORM (tolerant discriminator): 1 dot-alias request = the switch was clean (200, zero reactive involvement); 2 = the 400 fired once and the reactive strip recovered (200); >=3 = retry storm or strip loop = defect (S3).
POST-SWITCH ACCEPTED: the final dot-alias request reached 200.

BOUNDARY-MARKER RECORD (the S0/S2 discriminator): records every captured line carrying litellm boundary markers (encitem_*/litellm_enc:) — pre- vs post-switch comparison on review (see the recon_note): identical = same boundary (strip = S2 candidate); different = different deployments (strip justified = S0). recon — always records, never fails.
VERDICT RECORD: merged ndjson final text head (the post-switch terminal output, verbatim). recon — always records, never fails.
